title: Author Q+A: finprim is a Case for One Financial Validation Library in TypeScript
gist: finprim, an MIT-licensed zero-dependency TypeScript library (v0.1.4, 81 GitHub stars) unifying IBAN, BIC, card, sort code, VAT, routing and loan validation behind one API, was built after duplicated validators drifted across web and mobile; its author draws a hard line against becoming a payments or compliance engine.

insights.claim: finprim is an MIT-licensed TypeScript library unifying IBAN, BIC, card, sort code, VAT, routing number and loan calculations behind one API; at its fifth release, 0.1.4, the repository had 81 stars.
insights.speaker: Daniel Curtis
insights.so_what: Early-stage niche OSS; adoption signal is small.

insights.claim: Oluwatosin Adelaja built finprim after duplicated bank-detail validation at Sprint Technology Solutions drifted between web and mobile, causing valid details accepted on web to be rejected on mobile in a payout flow.
insights.speaker: Daniel Curtis
insights.so_what: Validation drift in fintech flows causes conversion loss and support costs.
insights.quote: nobody thinks to check whether two "identical" validators are actually identical

themes.theme: Design bets: one API, zero deps, branded types

insights.claim: finprim's bet is that financial validation is coherent enough for one consistent API, avoiding the glue code needed to reconcile multiple single-purpose packages with differing API shapes, types and dependencies.
insights.speaker: Daniel Curtis
insights.so_what: Consolidation of fragmented dev utilities reduces maintenance and supply-chain surface.

insights.claim: finprim ships with zero runtime dependencies so there is no dependency tree to audit or patch for code sitting in a payment path.
insights.speaker: Daniel Curtis
insights.so_what: Supply-chain risk minimization is a selling point in payments software.
insights.quote: For something sitting in the path of a payment, I wanted fewer moving parts, not more.

insights.claim: TypeScript branded types make a validated IBAN a distinct type from a plain string, moving 'forgot to validate this route' bugs from live transactions to compile time while runtime validation still runs.
insights.speaker: Daniel Curtis
insights.so_what: Type-level guarantees reduce production payment failures.

insights.claim: finprim stores nothing, makes no network calls, has no telemetry, and deliberately does not log sensitive account or card numbers; its author says it is not a compliance tool and does not tell you a payment is safe.
insights.speaker: Daniel Curtis
insights.so_what: Clear scope limits liability and positions it as complementary to payment providers.
insights.quote: Treating a validation library as more than that would be the real mistake.
insights.locator: Where I draw the line matters

insights.claim: finprim validates against published standards — ISO 13616 IBAN formats, Luhn plus card network ranges, documented per-country VAT formats — with overall coverage around 91% of lines and 88% of statements, and core validators around 94% of lines.
insights.speaker: Daniel Curtis
insights.so_what: Coverage split shows rigor concentrated where financial risk sits.

insights.claim: Keeping finprim's 80+ IBAN formats and VAT quirks current is mostly manual, with outside contributors in different countries surfacing edge cases.
insights.speaker: Daniel Curtis
insights.so_what: Maintenance burden is a key-person risk for single-maintainer financial OSS.

insights.claim: Adelaja says moving finprim into SEPA credit transfer or ACH batch generation would be a genuinely different job, and he wants it to remain a validation and formatting toolkit rather than a transaction engine or payments platform.
insights.speaker: Daniel Curtis
insights.so_what: Signals the library will not compete with payment providers.
insights.locator: Where I want finprim to sit

insights.claim: A DEV commenter warned that teams get burned when a money library's precision assumptions diverge from the payment processor's, while calling the Dinero.js approach solid.
insights.speaker: Daniel Curtis
insights.so_what: Precision mismatches between client libraries and processors are a real fintech failure mode.
insights.locator: Narrower tools exist, such as ibankit
